title: Metric Spiral Triage Runbook
content:
Quick summary: This is a practical runbook for investigating performance regressions using a "metric spiral" approach — start broad, collect signals across layers, then iteratively narrow to a small set of causal metrics and candidate commits. Focus areas: dashboards to snapshot, safe canary comparison steps, bisect-friendly experiment artifacts, and a short checklist for alert handoffs.

Context and motivation:
- We get noisy latency/throughput alerts that often come from downstream traffic patterns or cache warmup. Past incidents showed that chasing a single surface metric wastes cycles. The metric spiral is an explicit narrowing pattern: global SLOs -> surface service metrics -> model-level traces -> kernel/host counters.
- Audience: on-call SREs, serving runtime engineers, and first-line triage for perf regressions. Keep this intentionally lightweight so it can be used during paging.

1) Fast triage (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm signal: check APM alert and Grafana summary panel (Serving: P99 latency, QPS, errors). Capture the alert window (t0 = alert start, t1 = now).
- Snapshot: save a Grafana snapshot (perf-overview) and upload link to the incident thread.
- Quick cross-checks:
  - Is this global (all regions) or single region? (Grafana: by region panel)
  - Does a single model route account for spike? (Per-route latency heatmap)
  - Are error rates elevated? If yes, link to error traces.
- Initial owner: assign to eng-serving-runtime on-call. If from a dedicated/private customer, notify Solutions Eng / Customer Success immediately.

2) Metric Spiral – pruning sequence
- Level 0 (global): SLO deviation (P95/P99 increased), Request rate. Pull an aggregate timeseries for t0-2h..t1+30m.
- Level 1 (service surface): per-route latency, per-backend queue length, process_uptime, worker_count. Compare canary vs baseline windows.
- Level 2 (runtime internals): kvcache hit ratio, avg batch size, batching_latency_ms, kv_cache_eviction_rate.
- Level 3 (kernel/host): GPU utilization curves, PCIe errors, CPU steal, docker/image-level changes, driver version.
- Level 4 (model): sequence length distribution, kv-cache warmup per-token path, token occupancy heatmap.

Note: For each level, record a single 1-line delta: e.g., "kvcache_hit_ratio dropped 42% -> 21% in t0..t1". The goal is to produce an actionable hypothesis in 30–60 minutes.

3) Dashboards and queries to run (examples)
- Grafana panels to capture in every triage: Serving: P99 latency by route; Batching: avg batch size by model; KV: hit_ratio by instance; Host: GPU util by nodepool; Canary: delta panels (canary-baseline).
- PromQL snippets (examples):
  - p99_latency{job=\"serving\",route=~\".+\"} |> increase_over_time(1h)
  - sum(rate(requests_total{route=\"/generate\"}[5m])) by (model,instance)
  - (sum(kv_hits_total) / sum(kv_lookups_total)) by (instance)
- BigQuery ad-hoc (example): token-path histogram for a single request id range (useful when logs contain token-level timing).

4) Canary comparisons (safe workflow)
- Create a time-aligned snapshot: pick baseline window (t_base = t0-60m .. t0-30m) and canary window (t_can = t0 .. t0+30m) where t0 is when canary rollout started or when regression began.
- Use the "canary-diff" Grafana panels. Capture pairs for: p50/p95/p99 latency, avg batch size, kv hit rate, error rate, and QPS.
- Statistical check: if p99 delta > 15% AND kv_hit_rate delta < -10%, prioritize runtime cache regressions. Document thresholds in the incident ticket.
- If canary change is implicated, roll back canary and observe. Capture metrics pre/post rollback and attach to ticket.

5) Bisect-friendly artifacts to create before making changes (pre-emptive hygiene)
- Build artifact tagging: every nightly and prod image must include git SHA, build time, and kernel/driver version in /meta endpoint. Example: GET /meta -> {\"git_sha\":\"abc123\",\"cuda_ver\":\"12.1\"}.
- Keep a short reproducer dataset (10–50 inputs) with variable sequence lengths and long-tail tokens. Store in s3://redwood-triage/reproducers/ with naming scheme.
- Snapshot kernel profiles (nvprof/Nsight) for the failing time window and link them to the ticket.

6) Example bisect plan (when code change suspected)
- Hypothesis: change X in PR 1123 reduced size of batching window, causing smaller batches and higher per-token latency.
- Steps: a) Recreate baseline and candidate images (git SHAs). b) Spin a small cluster with equivalent traffic replay (shadow or replay tool) using reproducer set. c) Capture timing traces, batch size histograms, and kv cache stats. d) If candidate reproduces regression, run git-bisect between SHAs to find the offending commit. e) Attach perf traces to the commit.

7) Common fingerprints and suggested root causes
- Sharp drop in avg_batch_size + increase in p99: likely batching policy change or lazy coalescing bug.
- KV cache hit ratio drop with steady QPS: keyspace change, serialization change, or eviction policy.
- P99 latency bump correlated with GPU util drop: driver issue, kernel fallback, or host CPU CPU-starvation.
- Error spikes with no latency change: model decoding exceptions or input validation regressions.

8) Quick profiling checklist (collect these artifacts)
- Grafana snapshots and panels (list).
- Flamegraphs (per process) for the relevant interval.
- Batch size histograms for each model instance.
- KV cache stats: hits/lookups/evictions.
- Host-level metrics and dmesg/syslog for hardware signs.
- Container meta /image labels and runtime env.

9) Communication and handoff template (incident ticket blurb)
- One-liner problem: "P99 for /generate increased from 380ms -> 780ms at 2025-02-20T03:12Z; delta concentrated on model:starling-13b."
- Actions taken: short list (snapshots saved, initial hypothesis: batch size drop, rollbacks attempted).
- Next steps: who to page and suggested experiment (replay reproducer on candidate image, collect flamegraph).

10) Notes-to-self / open questions
- We lack a standardized small-replay harness that preserves batching behavior across clusters; building that will shave hours.
- Consider adding an automated canary-diff alert that computes a small set of diagnostic deltas (avg_batch_size, kv_hit_rate) and only pages if at least 2 of 3 are abnormal.
- Need a clearer memory of which models perform kernel-fallbacks when quantized under certain drivers — centralize this mapping.

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Replayer service (internal): tools/replayer -> usage: replayer --image sha --traffic s3://... --duration 10m
- Meta endpoint: curl http://<instance>/meta
- Grafana panels: perf-overview, per-route-latency, kv-cache-overview, batchizer-metrics, canary-diff
- Example PromQL stored in /ops/queries/perf_triage.prom

If anything in this runbook is unclear, ping @aisha (Slack) and add notes here. This is a working doc; please add postmortem artifacts and refine thresholds based on more incidents.

---
Unresolved: what is an RB-acceptable threshold for canary p99 delta when combined with host GPU metric noise? (TBD)
